### Q33. A new stoma becomes dusky and progressively dark. Which action is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Massage the stoma firmly
- **B.** Obtain urgent surgical or stoma specialist assessment for possible ischemia
- **C.** Cover it and wait until routine discharge
- **D.** Apply an unprescribed vasoconstrictor

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Obtain urgent surgical or stoma specialist assessment for possible ischemia**

Ischemia ka matlab tissue ko adequate blood supply na milna hai. New stoma ka progressively dark hona ischemia ya venous congestion ka warning sign ho sakta hai. Nurse appearance aur symptoms assess karke urgent surgical or stoma specialist review arrange karti hai. Delay se tissue viability compromise ho sakti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Firm massage blood supply safely restore nahi karta aur fragile mucosa injure kar sakta hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Urgent specialist assessment possible ischemia ko timely identify aur manage karne ke liye best hai.
- **C (Galat):** Routine discharge tak wait karna potentially serious complication ko delay karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Unprescribed vasoconstrictor blood vessels ko narrow kar sakta hai aur perfusion concern worsen kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Progressive dusky or black stoma = urgent surgical review.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/ostomy-surgery-bowel/complications).

### Q51. During manual disimpaction under an authorized plan, a patient becomes dizzy and bradycardic. What should the nurse suspect and do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Normal harmless response, continue forcefully
- **B.** A need to increase rectal pressure
- **C.** A sign that blood pressure must rise sharply
- **D.** Possible vagal stimulation, stop and assess circulation promptly

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Possible vagal stimulation, stop and assess circulation promptly**

Rectal manipulation se vagal reflex trigger ho sakta hai. Vagus nerve heart rate slow karne wale parasympathetic signals mein role play karti hai. Dizziness aur bradycardia ho toh manipulation stop karo, circulation aur vital signs assess karo aur urgent help lo. Disimpaction sirf authorized trained practice aur appropriate monitoring mein hoti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Symptomatic bradycardia harmless assume nahi karni chahiye. Force se injury aur instability badh sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Rectal pressure badhana reflex aur local tissue injury worsen kar sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bradycardia se blood pressure rise hona guaranteed nahi hai. Hypotension bhi ho sakti hai.
- **D (Sahi):** Vagal stimulation possible hai aur manipulation rokna further stimulation se bachata hai.

**Exam clue:** Rectal stimulation plus symptomatic bradycardia = stop and assess.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/27-4-common-conditions-affecting-bowel-elimination).

**Additional clinical reference:** [Relevant guidance](https://opentextbc.ca/pnapnsupplement/chapter/integrated-nursing-practice-1/).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q81. What appearance is expected of a healthy newly created intestinal stoma after initial assessment?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Dry black tissue
- **B.** Moist pink to red mucosa
- **C.** A deep blue hard surface
- **D.** Pale gray tissue without perfusion

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Moist pink to red mucosa**

Stoma surgically banaya gaya bowel opening hai. Healthy mucosa mein blood supply hoti hai, isliye surface generally moist pink ya red dikhti hai. Early postoperative swelling ho sakti hai, lekin progressive dusky, gray ya black change prompt assessment maangta hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Dry black tissue possible necrosis ka sign hai, normal viable mucosa nahi.
- **B (Sahi):** Moist pink-red mucosa adequate perfusion ke saath consistent hai.
- **C (Galat):** Deep blue hard appearance normal healthy mucosa ki expected finding nahi hai.
- **D (Galat):** Pale gray tissue without perfusion blood supply problem suggest karti hai.

**Exam clue:** Healthy stoma moist and pink-red. New darkening needs assessment.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/ostomy-surgery-bowel/complications).

### Q91. Which action protects peristomal skin when selecting an ostomy appliance?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Fit the opening closely around the stoma without constricting it
- **B.** Cut the opening smaller than the stoma to create pressure
- **C.** Leave a wide gap exposing skin to effluent
- **D.** Use ordinary adhesive directly on the stoma

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Fit the opening closely around the stoma without constricting it**

Peristomal skin stoma ke aas-paas ki skin hai. Bowel effluent skin ke contact mein aaye toh irritation aur breakdown ho sakta hai. Pouch barrier ka opening stoma ke size ke hisaab se close fit hona chahiye, bina mucosa ko compress kiye. Postoperative size changes ke liye remeasure karo aur appliance instructions follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Close nonconstricting fit skin exposure ko reduce karta hai aur stoma ko pressure se bachata hai.
- **B (Galat):** Too-small opening stoma par pressure aur tissue injury ka risk badhati hai.
- **C (Galat):** Wide gap se effluent skin par leak ho sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Ordinary adhesive directly mucosa par lagane se trauma aur poor seal ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Fit closely, not tightly. Measure again as swelling changes.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/ostomy-surgery-bowel/complications).

**Additional clinical reference:** [Relevant guidance](https://psag.wocn.org/index.html).

### Q2. A patient has stool leaking beneath the ostomy skin barrier and painful surrounding skin. What is the best intervention?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Assess skin and stoma fit and replace the leaking appliance appropriately
- **B.** Reinforce the leaking edge indefinitely without inspection
- **C.** Increase the appliance opening substantially in every case
- **D.** Apply harsh chemicals to irritated skin

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Assess skin and stoma fit and replace the leaking appliance appropriately**

Ostomy leakage se enzymes aur bowel contents surrounding skin ko irritate kar sakte hain. Painful skin ko inspect karo aur leakage ka cause, stoma size, skin folds aur appliance fit assess karo. Suitable barrier aur pouch replace karo, skin ko gentle care do aur persistent breakdown par ostomy specialist review lo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Skin aur fit assess karke leaking appliance replace karna actual leakage cause ko address karta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Leaking edge ko indefinitely reinforce karne se hidden skin damage continue ho sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Universal oversized opening skin exposure badha sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Harsh chemicals already irritated skin ko aur injure kar sakte hain.

**Exam clue:** Leakage means assess the seal and skin, not just add tape.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/ostomy-surgery-bowel/complications).

**Additional clinical reference:** [Relevant guidance](https://psag.wocn.org/index.html).

### Q34. Which position usually supports normal defecation for an ambulatory stable patient?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Sitting with appropriate foot support and privacy
- **B.** Standing on one foot
- **C.** Head-down tilt
- **D.** Flat supine with the legs rigid

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Sitting with appropriate foot support and privacy**

Normal defecation mein pelvic floor relaxation aur abdominal muscle coordination important hai. Stable ambulatory patient ko supported sitting, foot support, privacy aur sufficient time dena useful hai. Individual mobility, fall risk aur medical restrictions ke hisaab se assistance arrange karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Supported sitting aur privacy normal toileting mechanics aur comfort support karte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Ek pair par standing unstable hai aur defecation support nahi karti.
- **C (Galat):** Head-down tilt routine toileting posture nahi hai aur safety compromise kar sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Rigid flat posture normal toilet position ka benefit nahi deti.

**Exam clue:** Safe supported toileting and privacy promote elimination.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/27-2-factors-affecting-bowel-elimination).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q50. Which stool characteristic is generally expected from a functioning ileostomy compared with a distal colostomy?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Always fully formed dry stool
- **B.** More liquid or paste-like effluent
- **C.** Only blood in the bag
- **D.** No digestive content in the output

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. More liquid or paste-like effluent**

Ileostomy small intestine ke ileum se banayi jaati hai. Distal colostomy mein stool colon ke zyada hissa se guzarta hai jahan water absorb hota hai. Isliye ileostomy output generally softer, liquid ya paste-like hota hai. Diet, hydration aur adaptation se consistency change ho sakti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Fully formed dry stool ileostomy ka universal expected output nahi hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Liquid ya paste-like output distal colostomy ke comparison mein ileostomy ka expected pattern ho sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Blood-only output normal bowel effluent nahi hai. Significant bleeding assess karni chahiye.
- **D (Galat):** Ileostomy mein digestive contents aur fluid present hote hain.

**Exam clue:** More colon bypass = generally more liquid stool.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/27-1-gastrointestinal-tract-structures-and-functions).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q91. A patient with an ileostomy has markedly increased watery output and dizziness. Which concern is most important?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Expected absence of fluid loss
- **B.** A need to stop all drinking indefinitely
- **C.** Dehydration and electrolyte loss requiring assessment
- **D.** Fluid overload proven by increased output

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Dehydration and electrolyte loss requiring assessment**

Ileostomy mein colon ka water aur sodium absorption bypass hota hai. Markedly watery output se fluid aur sodium loss ho sakta hai. Dizziness, reduced urine aur low BP dehydration ke clues ho sakte hain. Nurse output, fluid balance, vitals aur ordered electrolyte/renal assessment review karke prompt clinical help leti hai. Fluid replacement plan individual condition ke mutabik hona chahiye.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Ileostomy output mein fluid loss hota hai. Isko absent assume karna galat hai.
- **B (Galat):** Sab fluids indefinitely rokne se dehydration worsen ho sakti hai. Specific fluid plan clinician decide karta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** High watery output ke saath dizziness fluid aur electrolyte loss ka important concern hai.
- **D (Galat):** Increased output alone fluid overload prove nahi karta. Volume depletion consider karni chahiye.

**Exam clue:** High ileostomy output plus dizziness = fluid and electrolyte assessment.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/digestive-diseases/ostomy-surgery-bowel/complications).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q69. Which method helps establish a bowel training routine when suitable?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Schedule toileting at consistent times, often after meals
- **B.** Use physical restraints during every toilet visit
- **C.** Change the schedule unpredictably each day
- **D.** Discourage the patient from responding to the urge

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Schedule toileting at consistent times, often after meals**

Gastrocolic reflex ka matlab meal ke baad colon ki activity badhna hai. Consistent toilet timing, often after meals, is natural reflex ka use kar sakti hai. Patient ke usual bowel habits, privacy, mobility aur safe access ko plan mein include karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Consistent timing patient ko routine develop karne aur meal-related bowel activity ka benefit lene mein madad karti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Physical restraint normal bowel training intervention nahi hai aur unnecessary harm kar sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Har din unpredictable timing se routine establish karna mushkil hota hai.
- **D (Galat):** Urge ignore karne se stool retention aur constipation ka risk badh sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** After-meal toileting can use the gastrocolic reflex.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/27-2-factors-affecting-bowel-elimination).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q78. A patient has frequent watery stools during antibiotic therapy. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Assess hydration, stool pattern and possible infectious causes and follow isolation or testing guidance
- **B.** Stop all oral fluids without clinical review
- **C.** Ignore because all antibiotic-associated diarrhea is harmless
- **D.** Give an antidiarrheal automatically before assessment

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Assess hydration, stool pattern and possible infectious causes and follow isolation or testing guidance**

Antibiotics gut ke normal microorganisms ko disturb kar sakti hain. Frequent watery diarrhea mein dehydration aur C. difficile infection consider karna chahiye, lekin har antibiotic-associated diarrhea CDI nahi hoti. Stool frequency, symptoms, hydration aur recent laxatives assess karo. Suspected infectious diarrhea mein local isolation, contact precautions aur indicated testing pathway follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Assessment aur indicated infection-control measures underlying cause aur transmission risk address karte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Bina indication oral fluids rokne se fluid deficit badh sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Antibiotic-associated diarrhea severe infection ya dehydration se related ho sakti hai. Ignore karna unsafe hai.
- **D (Galat):** Bina assessment automatic antidiarrheal dena infectious diarrhea mein inappropriate ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** New watery diarrhea on antibiotics: consider CDI, assess and follow precautions.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://www.cdc.gov/c-diff/hcp/clinical-overview/).

**Additional clinical reference:** [Relevant guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/c-diff/hcp/clinical-guidance/index.html).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q96. An immobile patient has frequent small liquid stools but a history of severe constipation. Which issue should be considered?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Absence of any stool retention
- **B.** Overflow around fecal impaction
- **C.** Normal complete emptying proven by liquid stool
- **D.** A definite need for antidiarrheal medication without assessment

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Overflow around fecal impaction**

Fecal impaction mein hard stool ka mass rectum ya lower colon mein atak sakta hai. Kabhi liquid stool hard mass ke aas-paas se leak hota hai, jise overflow diarrhea kehte hain. Isliye liquid stool dekh kar retention exclude mat karo. Bowel history, abdominal findings aur authorized assessment ke basis par care decide karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Stool retention possible hai aur assessment se hi clarify hoga.
- **B (Sahi):** Severe constipation ke saath small liquid stools overflow around impaction ka clue ho sakte hain.
- **C (Galat):** Liquid stool complete emptying prove nahi karta kyunki retained mass ke around leak ho sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Bina assessment antidiarrheal dene se underlying retention worsen ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Constipation history plus small watery leaks = consider overflow.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/27-4-common-conditions-affecting-bowel-elimination).

**Additional clinical reference:** [Relevant guidance](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sites/books/NBK448094/).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>

### Q107. What is the principal role of documenting bowel frequency, consistency and associated symptoms?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Predict all future bowel movements exactly
- **B.** Identify changes and guide individualized assessment and care
- **C.** Replace physical assessment in an acute abdomen
- **D.** Assign the same diagnosis to every patient

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Identify changes and guide individualized assessment and care**

Bowel documentation patient ka usual pattern aur current changes compare karne mein help karti hai. Frequency, consistency, color, amount, pain, blood, associated symptoms aur interventions ka response note karo as appropriate. Trends se individualized care aur escalation guide hoti hai, lekin records clinical assessment replace nahi karte.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Bowel records future movements exactly predict nahi kar sakte.
- **B (Sahi):** Accurate trends change detect karne aur patient-specific assessment plan banane mein help karte hain.
- **C (Galat):** Acute abdomen mein documentation alone sufficient nahi hai. Prompt physical and clinical assessment chahiye.
- **D (Galat):** Different patients mein same stool pattern ke different causes ho sakte hain. Universal diagnosis appropriate nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Document patterns and changes, then act on clinical red flags.

**Clinical reference:** [Topic reference](https://openstax.org/books/fundamentals-nursing/pages/27-4-common-conditions-affecting-bowel-elimination).

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** Specific coverage verification pending.

</details>
